messages:
olivia_ml: Quick canary update — ran a production-like slice for nova13b using INT8 weight-only variants from bitsandbytes and llm.int8. Wanted to surface ops + quality deltas before we widen the rollout.

olivia_ml: TL;DR: bnb path gives slightly better throughput and lower p95 on A100-40, but we saw small quality regressions on long-form QA and multi-turn summarization slices. llm.int8 is a hair slower and uses ~1.5GB more GPU memory but is more stable on a couple of sensitive slices.

raj_infra: what infra did you run on? batch sizes?

olivia_ml: A100-40GB nodes, single-stream clients, batch_size=1 typical for latency SLO, burst tests at batch=8. Warmup: 4 priming prompts for kv cache. Canary traffic config: 5% of canary slice, 1000 requests across slices.

olivia_ml: command we used:
```
python infra/benchmarks/throughput.py --model nova13b --quant bnb --batch 1 --gpu a100:0 --warmup 4 --tags canary_nov13b
python infra/benchmarks/throughput.py --model nova13b --quant llmint8 --batch 1 --gpu a100:0 --warmup 4 --tags canary_nov13b
```

gina_eval: quality numbers from the evaluation harness (slice names & delta = int8 - fp16 baseline):
- qa_longtail: bnb -1.1% EM, llm.int8 -0.4% EM
- summarize_multi_turn: bnb -1.8 RougeL, llm.int8 -0.7 RougeL
- short_factual: bnb +0.1, llm.int8 +0.2 (no sig change)
- code_completion_small: both within +/-0.2

gina_eval: confidence calibration: bnb has slightly overconfident responses on the QA slice (mean conf +0.06). We flagged 48 examples where hallucination increased.

simon_prod: latency numbers? p50/p95 for batch=1?

olivia_ml: measured on the same nodes behind the same routing: 
- bnb: p50 45ms, p95 78ms, tokens/sec ~115
- llm.int8: p50 52ms, p95 92ms, tokens/sec ~102
Memory resident (model + kv): bnb ~34.2GB, llm.int8 ~35.7GB

olivia_ml: note: bnb path used 8-bit optim kernels that avoid some copies; llm.int8 currently leverages a slightly different packing which increases resident by ~1.5GB.

kai_research: hypothesis: the quality gap on qa_longtail and multi_turn could stem from per-group scaling differences and quantization bias on softmax inputs. Worth running per-layer activation histograms and compare quant errors for the top layers.

kai_research: also want to try a very small fp16 fallback for attention layers only (hybrid) to see if that recovers the -1.8 RougeL without blowing up latency.

raj_infra: any ops regressions or increased errors?

olivia_ml: errors: slight increase in decode timeouts when we pushed batch=8 on bnb path (time window exceeded for a handful of requests) — probably need batching backpressure tuning. No OOMs, no GPU crashes.

deploy-bot: Canary status: canary_id=canary_1743219999, traffic split: 5% slice -> int8_bnb (70%), llm_int8 (30%). Alerts: none. Duration: 3h 20m.

simon_prod: thanks. action items?

olivia_ml: proposed next steps:
1) run per-layer quant error analysis (kai) and capture activation histograms for problematic examples.
2) run hybrid-attention fp16 experiment for bnb path (small change) and re-eval the two failing slices.
3) tune batching/backpressure for bnb to avoid timeouts at batch>=8 (raj).
4) expand canary to 15% after we get one of the above mitigations passing.

gina_eval: I'll prepare a focused eval harness that replays the 48 hallucination examples + 500 random longtail QA examples to get tighter CI.

kai_research: I'll start with layer-wise MSE and dynamic range checks, then post a short notebook.

raj_infra: I'll look at request tracing and backpressure metrics — suspect our batching window is too aggressive for the new kernels.

olivia_ml: if we recover >0.8 of the quality gap with hybrid attention, we can justify the bnb rollout for latency/cost reasons. Otherwise keep llm.int8 as default for this model.

simon_prod: please file a short ops note after the next run and tag me. Also include the canary config so we can audit the rollout policy.

olivia_ml: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
